questions.question_text: At what time of day is a gnomon sundial shadow shortest?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: At solar noon, when the Sun reaches its highest elevation in the sky.

questions.question_text: Explain how a gnomon shadow tracks time during a clear day.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Earth's rotation causes the Sun to appear to move from east to west. A vertical gnomon casts a long shadow pointing west at sunrise, shrinking to shortest length pointing north at solar noon, and lengthening toward east at sunset.

questions.question_text: Describe the orbital geometry corresponding to New Moon, First Quarter, and Full Moon phases.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. New Moon (Amavasya): Moon lies directly between Sun and Earth. The sunlit half faces away from Earth, rendering it invisible (0% lit). 2. First Quarter: Moon completes 1/4th orbit at 90 deg angle to Earth-Sun line. Half of the illuminated hemisphere is visible (50% lit). 3. Full Moon (Purnima): Earth lies between Sun and Moon. The entire sunlit hemisphere faces Earth, appearing as a complete circular disk (100% lit).

questions.marking_scheme_answer: No, the Moon is a non-luminous body. It reflects sunlight falling on its surface back toward Earth.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 11.2 Solar Shadow Gnomons and Sundials and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Earth's rotation causes Sun shadow movements across a gnomon stick, enabling sundial time tracking. Traditional Indian calendars combine lunar and solar cycles. [Heritage Note: Jantar Mantar Sundials] Massive stone gnomon instruments built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II measuring local solar time.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 11.1 Lunar Phases and Orbital Perspective and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The Moon produces no light of its own, shining by reflecting sunlight. Phases result from changing visible proportions of its sunlit hemisphere during its ~29.5 day orbit. [Think like a scientist: Why Moon Shapes Change] Half the Moon is always sunlit; our changing orbital perspective reveals varying lit portions.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 11.2 Solar Shadow Gnomons and Sundials and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Earth's rotation causes Sun shadow movements across a gnomon stick, enabling sundial time tracking. Traditional Indian calendars combine lunar and solar cycles. [Heritage Note: Jantar Mantar Sundials] Massive stone gnomon instruments built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II measuring local solar time.

questions.question_text: Explain how a gnomon sundial tracks solar time during a clear day.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: As Earth rotates on its axis from west to east, the Sun appears to move from east to west. A vertical gnomon stick casts a shadow pointing west at sunrise (long shadow), shrinking to shortest length pointing north at solar noon, and lengthening toward east at sunset.
